text:
You've imagined this moment often enough during the past three years. Its ancient towers rising above the Black Forest, its workshops and libraries, its illustrious professors, and the promise of learning a craft that could change your life.
An artificer. A proper one. Someone who can breathe intelligence into ink and parchment, and perhaps one day create something worth more than everything you've earned so far.
But first, a less inspiring form of magic.
The administrator slides a document across his desk.
"First-term tuition, Mr. Fibonacci. Payable in advance."
You glance at the sum.
Three years of savings. A remarkable amount of effort, about to disappear with a single signature.
Apparently, the first lesson at the Academy is that miracles are expensive.

args.successText: Somehow you talk him into a modest concession. He adjusts the figure with visible regret, and you leave the desk feeling only mostly robbed.
args.failureText: He hears you out, nods once, and leaves the total exactly where it was. You pay. Miracles remain expensive.

parameters.text: You pay the full sum without protest. The stamp falls; three years of savings become a neat entry in a ledger.

text:
Professor Glützenbaum is a small, elderly gentleman with a magnificent white moustache and spectacles that seem perpetually on the verge of sliding off his nose. He surveys the classroom with unconcealed satisfaction.

"Welcome, ladies and gentlemen! Today, you begin your journey toward becoming artificers. A noble profession, requiring intelligence, precision, patience, and a truly unreasonable tolerance for failure."

He produces a playing card from his pocket and places it on the lectern. The card promptly scuttles across the wood, stops at the edge, turns around, and comes back.

"Observe! A piece of cardboard that obeys instructions. Remarkable, isn't it? And this is merely a child's toy compared to the enchantments you may one day create."

He catches the card before it escapes again.

"But first, the foundations. All artificery draws upon four fundamental magical essences."

He gestures toward four colored sets of cards arranged on his desk.

"Green: life, growth, restoration, and the stubborn refusal of nature to stay properly organized."

"Blue: knowledge, perception, illusion, and the subtle art of knowing more than one ought."

"Red: energy, speed, chaos, and everything my colleagues wish I would stop demonstrating indoors."

"Black: structure, industry, preservation, and decay. The art of building things to last—or persuading them that they've lasted quite long enough."

He beams at the class.

"Each essence has its own properties, and every artificer develops particular affinities. You'll discover yours in time. For now, the Academy has kindly provided a selection of elementary decks."

He indicates the four sets.

"Choose whichever appeals to you. And don't fret over the decision! You'll study all four essences eventually."

neighbor_match.text:
Professor Glützenbaum claps his hands.

"Splendid! Now, the clever thing about these cards is that they already know how to play. They'll remember their own abilities, follow your instructions, and obey the rules without requiring a judge to inspect every move. Most of the time, anyway."

A few students laugh.

"Of course, designing such enchantments is considerably harder than using them. But we'll get to that soon enough."

He gestures toward the tables.

"For now, turn to your neighbor and have a friendly match. Experiment! Make mistakes! Discover what your cards can do!"

The young woman seated beside you turns with a warm, slightly shy smile.

"Hello! I'm Molly. Shall we give it a try?"

text:
The morning finds you in one of the Academy's artificery workshops, a curious mixture of classroom and laboratory. Rows of heavy wooden workbenches are cluttered with pigments, delicate instruments, glass vessels and mysterious brass contraptions. At the front stands Miss Lombard, a stern-looking woman in her forties, whose immaculate appearance suggests that even the dust in this room knows better than to misbehave.

"Good morning. I am Professor Lombard, and I shall be teaching you artificery. Yesterday, you learned to play with enchanted cards. Today, you shall begin learning to make them."

She pauses to let the distinction sink in.

"An artificer must be able to bind magical essences into a precise, stable creation. We shall begin with Conjuration: shaping a card from raw materials through intuition and experimentation. The result may surprise you. Indeed, you may discover enchantments you do not yet understand, which you will eventually learn to reproduce deliberately."

She picks up a blank card and places it on her desk.

"Remember: the purpose of these exercises is not merely to produce better playing cards. Every technique you master here is a step toward creating the sophisticated magical artifacts upon which our profession is built."

A young man sitting beside you leans over with a friendly smile. He has an easy confidence about him, and an accent you cannot quite place.

"She's quite right, you know. My family has been crafting enchanted objects for generations. Back home, a reliable magical advisor can fetch more than a merchant's entire cargo. And here we are, learning to make pieces of cardboard chase one another across a table."

He gives a delighted chuckle.

"Ousmane, by the way. Ousmane Tempeli. I came all this way to discover what these northern Academies know that we don't. With any luck, something worth bringing home."

Before you can reply, Miss Lombard clears her throat.

"Mr. Tempeli. I trust your conversation is contributing to the education of the entire class?"

"Not yet, Professor. But I have every confidence it will."

A few students laugh. Miss Lombard does not.

"How reassuring. Then perhaps you and Mr. Fibonacci would care to begin your work."

Ousmane gives you a cheerful wink as he turns toward his materials.

"Well, Antonio. Shall we see what wonders we can produce?"

parameters.title: Family and ambitions
parameters.description: Ousmane Tempeli is a warm, confident young man from a distinguished family of artificers in a distant southern country. He came to the Academy to discover unfamiliar techniques and bring valuable knowledge home. He has practical familiarity with the commercial world of magical artifacts.

text:
"That was fun! You're quite good at this, aren't you?"
She gathers her cards, carefully stacking them into a neat pile.
"It's funny, isn't it? All those little enchantments, just to make some cardboard follow the rules of a game. And apparently this is the easy part!"
She laughs.
"My father once met an artificer whose cards could actually give advice. Proper conversations, I mean. Imagine being clever enough to make something like that!"
title: A Friendly Face

parameters.title: Fellow student
parameters.description: Molly is a friendly, modest fellow student who seems uncertain of her academic abilities.

text:
As you go back to your room, you pass through the library. It is settling into its evening silence, except for one table that seems determined to resist the process. Three children are gathered around a young woman with kind eyes and a rather tired smile. One is struggling with a page of arithmetic, another is constructing a tower out of books, and the third is earnestly explaining why his homework was eaten by a goat.

"Well, that is unfortunate," the young woman says, apparently taking the goat's involvement quite seriously. She looks up as you approach. "Oh, hello Anotnio! I'm Molly, you remember? Are we being too loud? We can move somewhere else."

You assure her that you aren't here to complain. Relieved, she explains that the children come from families in the nearby village, and that she helps them with their lessons in the evenings. "Some of them can't afford proper schooling. It's only a little thing, really." She glances at the growing tower of books. "Though it's becoming rather more than a little thing. I have my own studies to keep up with, and there are more children coming every week."

The tower collapses with a magnificent thud. Molly closes her eyes for a moment, then patiently begins gathering the books.

"I've been thinking I should find someone to help. A fellow student, perhaps. I'd pay them, of course. It wouldn't be fair otherwise." She smiles at you. "You wouldn't happen to know anyone who might be interested?"

parameters.text:
"Well, I could help," you suggest.

Molly brightens immediately. "Really? Oh, that would be wonderful! Are you good with children?"

Before you can answer, the smallest boy looks you up and down. "Do you know your multiplication tables?"

An interview. Already.

Molly gives you an apologetic smile. "They're very thorough."

job.name: Library Mentoring
job.description: Help younger students at the library under Molly's guidance.

parameters.text:
"Actually, I know someone who might be perfect. Emma Delamain. She's brilliant, very serious about her studies, and I think she'd make an excellent teacher. Just, err... Don't tell her I said that."

"Emma Delamain?" Molly repeats thoughtfully. "I don't think we've met. Do you think she'd be interested?"

You admit that you haven't asked her.

"Well, perhaps I could speak to her sometime." Molly smiles. "Thank you, Antonio. That's very kind of you."

From beneath the table, a small voice announces that the goat has eaten another assignment.

"It sounds like a wonderful thing you're doing. I hope you find someone to help."

"Thank you." Molly's smile is warm, if a little weary. "They're good children, really. Even when they aren't being especially good."

One of the children proudly presents her with a drawing of a dragon. It has six legs, three heads, and what appears to be a very large moustache.

"Oh, that's lovely!" she says, with complete sincerity.

title: The Little Scholars

parameters.title: Village tutor
parameters.description: Molly volunteers to tutor children from poor families in the nearby village. She is kind, patient, and increasingly overwhelmed by the work.

title: The Running Lesson
text:
The Academy apparently believes that a sound mind requires sound legs. Today's afternoon lesson therefore takes place in the courtyard, where a physical-training instructor has ordered the students to run laps around the grounds. You join the procession, trying to decide whether this counts as education or an elaborate punishment.

A few strides ahead, Molly is in magnificent spirits. She runs with an easy, springy gait, chatting to Emma as though the two of them were enjoying a leisurely walk through a garden.

"And then I told the stable boy that of course he could bring the foal indoors, just until the rain stopped—oh, Antonio! Hello! Isn't this lovely?"

She waves enthusiastically and, without noticing, picks up the pace. Emma follows with considerably less enthusiasm. Her face is composed, but her breathing suggests that composing it is taking a heroic effort.

"Lovely," Emma manages. "An inspired word for... running in circles."

Molly laughs. "Oh, you'll feel wonderful afterward! It's just a matter of finding your rhythm."

Emma looks at you. It is a remarkable look: simultaneously a request for mercy and a warning not to enjoy this too much.

parameters.text:
"Race you to the gate, Molly!"

Her eyes light up. "Really? Oh, splendid!"

She surges forward. You follow, somehow finding another reserve of speed, and the two of you thunder past the fountain almost shoulder to shoulder. At the gate you make one final, desperate effort and reach the stone post a fraction ahead of her.

Molly stops, breathless and delighted. "Antonio! That was wonderful! I didn't know you could run like that!" She gives your shoulder an approving squeeze. "We absolutely must train together. I run on Monday evenings, here in the courtyard. You should come!"

Behind you, Emma arrives at a more dignified pace. "Congratulations," she says between breaths. "You've both successfully reached a gate. Truly, a historic day for scholarship."

Molly greets you with a grin. "I still think about that race to the gate, Antonio. You were fast! Next time I'm not letting you sneak ahead in the last few steps." She looks rather pleased at the prospect of a rematch.

"Race you to the gate, Molly!"

"Oh! All right!" Molly brightens immediately, and then—rather alarmingly—accelerates.

For several glorious seconds you keep up. Then your lungs begin making objections that your legs can no longer ignore. By the time you reach the gate, Molly is already waiting, bouncing lightly on her heels.

"That was fun!" she declares, entirely without condescension. "You started so quickly! Perhaps we should work on keeping that pace. I run here on Monday evenings. Come train with me!"

Emma catches up, takes one look at you, and produces a small, exhausted smile. "Well. At least one of us had the sense to stop competing with her."

Molly waves cheerfully. "Have you recovered from our race? I hope I didn't go too fast. Come along on Monday—we'll get you into splendid shape." Her expression suggests that this is a promise, not a threat.

You fall into step beside Molly and lower your voice. "I think Emma might appreciate a slightly more leisurely pace."

Molly glances over her shoulder. Emma is several strides back, pursuing the conversation with the grim determination of someone pursuing an escaping carriage.

"Oh!" Molly slows at once. "Emma, I'm so sorry! I didn't even notice!"

"No apology necessary," Emma says, drawing alongside you. "I was merely considering whether the Academy offers correspondence courses in physical education."

Molly giggles, then turns to you with an appreciative smile. "Thank you for telling me, Antonio. I do get carried away. You know, I run here on Monday evenings. Would you like to join me sometime? We could go at whatever pace suits you."

Emma gives you the faintest nod of gratitude. It's the sort of gesture that might be missed by anyone who hadn't just saved her from another lap at Molly's preferred speed.

"I'm glad you told me to slow down for Emma that day," Molly says. "Sometimes I get so excited that I forget other people aren't enjoying themselves quite as much as I am." She smiles. "Although I do hope you enjoyed it a little!"

parameters.text:
You drift back beside Emma. "Come on, Delamain. I thought you excelled at everything. Don't tell me a few laps have finally uncovered your weakness."

She gives you a murderous sideways glance, somewhat spoiled by the fact that she is too short of breath to accompany it with a proper reply.

"I'm... conserving... my brilliance," she says at last. "For pursuits... that matter."

"Then perhaps we should enter you in the Academy's slowest-moving carriage competition."

"Fibonacci, when I can breathe again, you are going to regret this."

Molly drops back beside you, looking from one to the other. "Oh, don't tease her! Emma's doing wonderfully!" She pauses, then her face brightens. "Actually, I have a marvelous idea. I run here on Monday evenings. Why don't you both come? It would be much more fun together!"

Emma stares at her. Then at you. "Wonderful," she says flatly. "A conspiracy."

Molly beams. Apparently that settles it.
"Are you coming running with us again?" Molly asks brightly. "Emma says she's only doing it to prove a point." A brief pause. "I'm not quite sure what point, but I'm very proud of her."

Emma regards you with a cool smile. "Ah, Fibonacci. Come to make another contribution to my athletic education? I assure you my stamina has improved. My tolerance for your commentary remains unchanged."

text:
You encounter Molly in the Academy courtyard just as she's finishing an afternoon of exercise. Her hair has escaped its ribbon, her cheeks are pink, and she looks entirely too pleased with herself for someone who has apparently spent the last hour being thrown about on a patch of grass.

"Antonio!" She hurries over and takes your hand in greeting. Her grip is firm. Very firm. For one alarming instant, you wonder whether the Academy has secretly installed a mechanical hand beneath her sleeve.

"Good heavens, Molly. Do you crack walnuts with that thing?"

"Sometimes!" She laughs. "Well, not often. It's rather messy."

She notices you flexing your fingers and looks suddenly apologetic. "Oh! Did I squeeze too hard? I'm sorry. I've been practicing wrestling since I was little. My father's guards taught me. They said I was too small to manage the larger boys, so naturally I had to prove them wrong."

Her embarrassment gives way to a mischievous smile. "Actually, I think I could take you."

You look at this cheerful young woman, considerably smaller than you, with her loose hair and innocent expression. One doesn't often receive such a generous invitation to make a fool of oneself.

"Would you like to try?" she asks eagerly. "Just a friendly bout! First to pin the other's shoulders, and no rough stuff."

parameters.text:
You agree, and Molly immediately shows you where to stand. She's surprisingly serious about the rules: no striking, no dangerous holds, and the moment either of you taps out, the match ends. Then she offers a bright smile. "Ready?"

You are barely ready before she comes at you. Her first move is so quick that you stumble, and only a desperate shift of balance keeps you upright. Molly laughs, delighted, and tries to take your leg. This time you anticipate her, turn with the movement, and manage to bring her down onto the grass.

For a moment you find yourselves in an absurd tangle of limbs. Molly attempts to escape with a strength that seems altogether unreasonable for her size, but you manage to pin both shoulders before she can roll free.

"Oh!" She blinks up at you, then bursts out laughing. "You got me! Properly got me!"

You release her and help her up. She accepts your hand with a grin, brushes grass from her clothes, and shakes yours solemnly—as though the two of you have just concluded an important international treaty.

"I owe you a prize!" She rummages through the small satchel beside the practice ground and produces a card. "There. A victory deserves something. And don't think this means I won't ask for a rematch."
Molly beams when she sees you. "I've been practicing that move you used against me, Antonio. You won't catch me with it twice!" She thinks for a moment. "Well. Probably not twice."

You agree, and Molly carefully explains the rules: no striking, no dangerous holds, and an immediate stop if either person taps out. "All right? Good! Ready?"

She takes hold of your arm. The next few seconds are difficult to reconstruct. The sky rotates. Your feet appear in a place where your head had been a moment earlier. And then you are lying on the grass with Molly firmly but harmlessly pinning your shoulders.

"One, two, three!" she announces triumphantly.

She realizes how close your faces are, and a blush rises to her cheeks. "Oh. Hello!"

"Hello," you reply. From this position, dignity is proving difficult to maintain.

Molly scrambles up and offers you her hand. "Sorry! I got a bit carried away. Are you all right?" She helps you to your feet, still smiling. "You nearly had me at the beginning, you know. If you learn to keep your balance when I turn, you'll be much harder to throw."

You're not entirely certain you were nearly anywhere except on the ground, but her encouragement is sincere.

Molly gives you an encouraging smile. "You really must wrestle with me again sometime! I've thought of a few things we can practice so you don't go flying quite so quickly." She pauses. "Sorry. That sounded worse than I meant it."

title: The Gentle Art of Wrestling

dinner_invitation.text:
Molly retrieves her belongings and glances toward the Academy buildings. "All this exercise has made me terribly hungry. Oh! Why don't you come to dinner with me? I live at the Royal Pigeon Inn. Their dining room is wonderful, and the cook makes the most marvelous roast potatoes."

She gives your arm an affectionate squeeze. "The next evening we're both free. My treat! We can celebrate our match, and you can tell me how your studies are going."

She looks at you expectantly. The invitation seems entirely sincere, with none of Emma's carefully calculated ambiguity. Of course, whether it is only dinner is another question.

parameters.text:
"I'd love to. Especially if the roast potatoes are as good as you say."

"Oh, they are!" Molly's face lights up. "I'll ask them to save us a nice table. And you must try the chocolate pudding! Actually, perhaps we should start with that. No, that would be silly."

She considers the matter with great seriousness.

"We'll see how hungry we are."

You leave her happily planning a meal that threatens to require more endurance than the wrestling match.

"I'd be delighted," you say. "Although I was rather hoping you might let me take you to dinner as a date. A proper one."

Molly stops adjusting the strap of her satchel. "A date? With me?"

For once, she seems unable to decide what to do with her hands. Then she smiles, a little shyly but with unmistakable pleasure.

"Oh, Antonio. Yes, I'd like that very much." She glances at you, and a mischievous spark returns to her eyes. "Although I should warn you, if you intend to impress me by wrestling again, I may insist on a rematch before dessert."

Molly looks at you with a shy, delighted smile. "You know, I thought we were just going to have dinner after our wrestling match. I didn't expect you to ask me on a proper date." She laughs softly. "I'm very glad you did."

"I'd be delighted. In fact, perhaps we could make it a date?"

Molly blinks. Her smile doesn't disappear, but she takes a moment before answering.

"Oh! That's sweet of you, Antonio." She blushes. "I really would like to have dinner together. I'm just not quite ready to call it a date. We haven't known each other very long, have we?"

She touches your arm reassuringly. "But please do come! I'd hate for you to miss those roast potatoes on account of a misunderstanding."

You agree that roast potatoes deserve to be considered on their own merits.

dinner_invitation.title: An Invitation

text:
The cafeteria is busy when Molly spots you coming through the door. She waves so vigorously that two students turn around to see whom she's greeting.

"Antonio! Just the person I wanted!" She hurries over, glowing with excitement. "Would you like to spend the night with me?"

A spoon clatters onto a plate at the next table.

Well. That is unusually direct.

_She means an evening together,_ you tell yourself. _Perhaps a late supper._

Of course. A perfectly sensible interpretation. And yet she did say _the night_.

Molly doesn't notice your sudden interest in precise vocabulary. "I've been planning it for days! I've already bought the chocolate, and there are plenty of pillows. You won't need to bring a thing."

The conversation around you seems to have developed an unexpected interest in silence. A young man behind Molly raises his eyebrows so high they threaten to disappear into his hair.

_Chocolate. Pillows. Her room._

Steady, Fibonacci. You have known this girl for approximately five minutes in the grand scheme of human relationships. There must be some innocent explanation.

"At the Royal Pigeon," she adds helpfully. "My room's quite large. And don't worry, I have something you can wear!"

An innocent explanation is becoming distressingly difficult to construct.

Around you, several students are now listening with shameless attention. Molly glances at them, then back at you. "So? Would you like to come?"

You are rapidly acquiring a reputation without having made a single decision. Which, admittedly, is an efficient way to acquire one.

parameters.text:
"I... yes. I'd be delighted."

"Wonderful!" Molly clasps her hands. "Come by after supper. Margaret says we mustn't make too much noise, so naturally we'll have to be very quiet."

_Very quiet._ You nod with what you hope is a worldly, unflustered expression.

You may wish to practice that expression before the evening. The cafeteria, judging by the smirks, has found the present version unconvincing.

Emma greets you with a smile of such exquisite innocence that you immediately suspect trouble.

"Antonio! I hear congratulations are in order. Apparently, Molly invited you to spend the night in her bedroom. In front of half the cafeteria, no less!"

You attempt to explain, but Emma raises a hand.

"Please, Fibonacci. Your private affairs are entirely your own. I would never dream of prying."

She pauses, visibly savoring the moment.

"Although I must say, I rather admire Molly's efficiency. Some girls spend weeks dropping hints. She simply announces her intentions over lunch."

There is absolutely no point arguing. Emma has found a new source of entertainment, and she intends to enjoy it.

"Thank you, Molly, but I don't think I can make it."

"Oh, what a pity!" She looks genuinely disappointed, but only for a moment. "I thought you'd enjoy a pajama party. We used to have such fun with pillow fights and hot chocolate when I was little! Never mind. I'll save you some chocolate if there's any left. Although I can't promise there will be."

_A pajama party._ Ah.

She gives your hand a quick affectionate squeeze and goes off to tell the next unfortunate acquaintance about her evening plans. The cafeteria's audience, robbed of its scandal, returns reluctantly to lunch.
Molly smiles when you mention her party. "The hot chocolate was delicious! I did make rather too much, though. I wish you could have joined me, Antonio. Perhaps another time?"
