parameters.text: "I've been examining our notes from the Forest of Schlupak," Emma says. "Crimson mushrooms, treacherous ground, and a truly unreasonable number of ways to fall into trouble." You suggest she could have collected safer ingredients. "Where would the scientific merit be in that?" She gives you a challenging smile. "Besides, I did bring a companion. One ought to test the reliability of one's field assistants."

title: The Dreaming Hollow
text:
"Antonio, do you remember our little expedition to the Forest of Schlupak?"

Emma produces a new map before you can reply.

"I've discovered something rather intriguing. There's an ancient hollow deep in the forest where two exceptionally rare magical substances can be found. I propose we investigate."

She looks at you with a smile.

"And this time, I've brought considerably better equipment."

Your second expedition takes you deeper into Schlupak than before. Eventually, the trees give way to an enormous hollow oak, its interior illuminated by an eerie blue-green light.

Inside, enormous translucent spheres hang suspended among the branches, slowly pulsing with pale violet light. Beneath them, clusters of delicate mushrooms release clouds of iridescent spores.

Emma stops dead.

"Oh, that's magnificent."

She approaches a floating sphere, examining it with obvious fascination.

"Schlupak Dreamspheres. Concentrated oneiric energy! Their magical properties are extraordinary. They're particularly useful for enchantments that manipulate the behavior of other spells and creatures."

Then she notices the mushrooms.

"And below them... Schlupak Spores. Equally valuable, but with very different properties. They enhance magical circulation and displacement. Excellent for drawing cards and returning summoned creatures to their owner's hand."

She begins unpacking her equipment.

"There's a complication, naturally."

She points toward the spheres.

"Disturbing a Dreamsphere causes the surrounding spores to disperse. But harvesting the spores destabilizes the spheres, making them dissolve."

Emma considers the problem for a moment, then shrugs.

"We can safely collect two specimens of either substance. Not both."

She looks at you.

"Well, Antonio? Which would be more useful for your next masterpiece?"

parameters.text:
You choose the floating spheres.

Emma nods approvingly and produces a curious glass instrument resembling a butterfly net designed by an astronomer.

"Excellent. Carefully, now. They're extremely sensitive to sudden movements."

Under her guidance, you capture two of the shimmering spheres. Their surfaces ripple gently as you lower them into protective containers.

The remaining spheres begin to fade, releasing a soft burst of light that scatters the spores throughout the hollow.

Emma holds up one of your acquisitions.

"Beautiful. Just think of the possibilities! Mesmerizing enemies, manipulating their actions, disrupting entire formations..."

Her expression grows thoughtful.

"Do remind me never to play against you without a suitable counterspell."

You indicate the clusters of mushrooms beneath the branches.

"The spores? Interesting."

Emma produces a small bellows and two sealed glass vessels.

"Very well. We shall have to be delicate. These things are extraordinarily sensitive to air currents."

She demonstrates a careful technique for gathering the spores without scattering them, then hands you the instrument.

After several minutes of painstaking work, both vessels are filled with shimmering powder.

Above you, the Dreamspheres begin to tremble, then dissolve into a gentle shower of violet sparks.

Emma examines your harvest with satisfaction.

"Excellent. With this much material, you could develop some truly remarkable circulation enchantments. Faster card recovery, magical displacement, perhaps even some interesting combinations."

She seals the vessels.

"And unlike certain other specimens we've encountered in this forest, these have made no attempt whatsoever to poison us."

manualTrigger: Emma has another proposal — Forest of Schlupak

parameters.text: "That hollow in the forest still troubles me," Emma admits. "Floating Dreamspheres on one side, rare spores on the other, and no way to collect everything without damaging something." You remind her that they chose. "Yes, and I stand by it." She pauses. "Mostly. It's the sort of dilemma that makes a scientist want to return with twice the equipment and no one telling her to be sensible."

title: The Price of High Society
text:
You and Emma are leaving the Academy when a familiar voice calls after you.

"Emma! Antonio! Just the two people I was hoping to find."

Elsa Falkenstein approaches, looking particularly pleased with herself. She carries an elegant envelope, sealed with crimson wax.

"I'm hosting my birthday celebration at the Royal Pigeon Inn next Saturday. A proper reception, naturally. Music, dancing, an excellent dinner, and a rather distinguished guest list."

She hands Emma the envelope.

"I would very much like you to attend, Emma. Your little successes at the Academy have attracted quite a bit of attention lately. I think you'll find the company interesting, and I'm sure my guests will be delighted to meet you."

Emma studies the invitation, mildly surprised.

"How very gracious of you, Elsa."

"Naturally. And Antonio, I have a rather different role in mind for you."

Elsa's smile widens.

"I'm going to need an additional waiter."

There is a short silence.

"A waiter?" you repeat.

"Yes, darling. You do have experience in hospitality, don't you? And I've already arranged a proper uniform for you. White gloves, a splendid black coat, the works. You'll look positively magnificent."

Emma presses her lips together. You recognize the expression. She is making a considerable effort not to smile.

{{ invitation_terms }}

variants.text:
"Now, before you object," Elsa continues, "I believe we had an agreement. A certain little favor, in exchange for some rather valuable information about my brother."

Ah.

You remember that agreement. You remember expressing certain reservations about it, too.

Emma inclines her head.

"Quite right, Elsa. A promise is a promise."

"How refreshing! I knew I could count on you both."

Elsa looks positively radiant.

"And don't worry, Antonio. I assure you the uniform is of the very finest quality."

invitation_terms.fallback:
"Of course, I wouldn't dream of imposing on you without compensation," Elsa adds pleasantly. "Two hundred crowns each. For one evening. I think you'll agree that's a generous offer."

Emma raises an eyebrow.

"Two hundred each? That's rather extravagant for a birthday party."

"My dear Emma, I intend this to be an occasion people remember. Good company is worth paying for."

She turns toward you.

"Well, Antonio? What do you say?"

parameters.text:
"Well, a deal is a deal," you concede.

"Precisely!" Elsa claps her hands, delighted.

You turn toward Emma.

"Remind me, whose brilliant idea was it to owe Elsa a favor?"

Emma regards you with complete composure.

"I believe we agreed it was an excellent strategic decision at the time."

"Did we?"

"We obtained the information, didn't we?"

Elsa watches the exchange with evident satisfaction.

"Oh, this is going to be such a lovely evening."

"Two hundred crowns for an evening's work? Very well. You have yourself a waiter."

"Splendid!" Elsa beams. "I knew you'd be reasonable."

Emma looks at you with amused disbelief.

"Antonio Fibonacci, bought for two hundred crowns. I shall remember this."

"Coming from someone who just accepted two hundred crowns for attending a party, that's rather rich."

"Ah, but I'm attending as a guest. You're serving drinks."

Elsa looks from one to the other, clearly enjoying herself.

"Wonderful. Now, about your measurements..."

"Thank you, Elsa, but I think I'll decline. Two hundred crowns is tempting, but I didn't come to the Academy to spend my evenings serving drinks."

Elsa looks briefly disappointed.

"Oh, what a pity. I was so looking forward to seeing you in the uniform."

"I'm sure you were."

Emma gives you an approving glance.

"A perfectly reasonable decision, Antonio. Though I confess, I'm a little disappointed myself."

"About the money?"

"About the uniform, naturally."

Elsa sighs.

"Well, I'll simply have to find someone else. Emma, darling, I do hope you'll still come."

Emma considers the invitation.

"Why not? It sounds like an interesting evening."

Elsa brightens at once, and the two young women begin discussing the guest list, leaving you with the uncomfortable realization that your refusal has deprived you of precisely one thing: an opportunity for Emma to laugh at your expense.

birthday_party.text:
The Royal Pigeon Inn has been transformed for the occasion. Chandeliers glitter above elegantly dressed guests, a small orchestra plays near the windows, and liveried servants glide between the tables bearing silver trays of delicacies.

Elsa has spared no expense. To her credit, the result is magnificent.

You, meanwhile, are standing in a servants' room, contemplating your reflection in a mirror.

The uniform is magnificent too, in its own way. A stiff black tailcoat, a brilliant white waistcoat, an enormous bow tie, immaculate white gloves, and a collar so high that turning your head has become a complicated operation.

You look like a penguin that has inherited a title.

The head waiter inspects you, adjusts your bow tie by a fraction of an inch, and hands you a silver tray.

"Sparkling wine. The ladies at the table by the window."

You take the tray and make your way through the reception.

There, seated together in elegant evening dresses, are Emma and Molly. The two friends are enjoying themselves enormously, laughing over some private conversation.

Emma notices you first.

Her expression freezes.

Her eyes travel slowly from your polished shoes to the tails of your coat, then upward to the magnificent bow tie.

She presses a hand to her mouth.

Molly turns to see what has caught her attention.

"Oh! Antonio! You look so..."

Molly stops, searching desperately for a suitable adjective.

"...professional!"

That does it.

Emma lets out a small, strangled sound. She attempts to disguise it as a cough, then as a sip from her glass, but the effort is hopeless. Her shoulders begin to shake.

"Emma," you say with as much dignity as your collar permits, "may I offer you some sparkling wine?"

She tries to answer. She truly does.

"Thank you, Antonio, that's very..."

Her eyes meet yours.

"...very..."

And then she loses the battle entirely.

She bursts into helpless laughter, bending forward with one hand over her face. Molly, caught between sympathy for you and the contagious absurdity of the situation, begins giggling too.

For perhaps half a minute, Emma is quite incapable of speech.

At last, she manages to recover enough composure to accept a glass.

"Oh, Antonio!" She wipes a tear from the corner of her eye. "Forgive me. It's just... that bow tie! And the way you're standing!"

"Madam," you reply stiffly, "I am merely endeavoring to provide the highest standard of service."

This proves to be a serious mistake.

Emma collapses into laughter again.

Molly reaches across the table to pat your hand sympathetically.

"I think you look very handsome, Antonio. Really!"

"Thank you, Molly."

Emma raises her glass, still struggling to contain herself.

"To Antonio Fibonacci," she declares, "the most distinguished gentleman ever to carry a tray!"

You give an elaborate bow, to the evident delight of both ladies, and retreat with what remains of your dignity.

Across the room, Elsa watches the scene with a satisfied little smile. Her party is going splendidly.

And judging by the laughter still coming from the table by the window, it is certainly going to be remembered.
birthday_party.title: A Most Distinguished Waiter

parameters.text: "Elsa's birthday invitation was a masterpiece," Emma says dryly. "One part celebration, two parts social obligation, and just enough menace to make the stationery memorable." You ask whether she's looking forward to the party. "I'm looking forward to discovering what she expects of us." Her smile is perfectly polished. "If there are refreshments, I shall consider them partial compensation."

title: An Evening's Entertainment
text:
The Old Monk Inn is unusually lively tonight. Its common room is crowded with merchants, travelers, and townsfolk enjoying their supper. Above the cheerful clatter of glasses and conversation, a violin is playing.

And playing beautifully.

You follow the music toward the far end of the room, where a young woman stands beside the fireplace, her bow moving effortlessly across the strings. The melody is lively and intricate, drawing delighted smiles from the guests.

Emma Delamain.

Of course. Is there _anything_ this woman cannot do?

She finishes with a magnificent flourish, and the room bursts into applause. Several coins find their way into a little wooden bowl beside her chair.

Emma accepts the appreciation with a graceful bow. Then she spots you.

"Antonio! What a pleasant surprise." Her eyes brighten with an idea. "Tell me, do you have any plans for the evening?"

Before you can answer, she gestures toward the crowded room.

"The innkeeper lets me perform here occasionally. The pay isn't magnificent, but the tips are respectable, and apparently the guests prefer my violin to his nephew's bagpipes."

She glances at the growing crowd.

"Unfortunately, I seem to have become rather popular tonight. Would you care to make yourself useful? I could do with someone to collect requests, carry drinks, and ensure my admirers remember where to leave their coins."

She offers you an innocent smile.

"Consider it an opportunity to participate in the arts."

parameters.title: Music and livelihood
parameters.description: Emma is a virtuoso violinist, the result of years of dedicated practice. She occasionally performs at the Old Monk Inn to earn money for her living expenses. Unlike most Academy students, she cannot rely on family wealth and must work alongside her studies.

parameters.text: "You looked rather surprised when you found me playing at the Old Monk Inn," Emma remarks. You admit you hadn't known about her violin. "A grave omission in your research, Fibonacci." She rests her fingers lightly on the instrument case. "I don't talk about it as often as artificery. Sometimes it's nice to be good at something simply because I love it." She smiles. "Though I don't object to applause."

"Have you heard Emma Delamain play the violin?" the speaker asks. "She performed at the Old Monk Inn, and she was remarkable. Who knew the Academy's fearsome artificer could make something sound so beautiful without enchanting a single card?" There is a small, appreciative pause. "Worth hearing if you ever get the chance."

"Very well. I've worked in an inn before. How difficult can it be?"

"Splendid! I knew I could rely on your extensive professional qualifications."

She presses a serving tray into your hands.

"Now, the gentleman in the green coat has requested something cheerful, the merchant by the window insists on a traditional ballad, and the table near the stairs has ordered another round of wine."

She pauses.

"Oh, and Antonio? Do try not to accept any requests for bagpipes."

"I think I'll leave the professional entertainment to you. Someone has to appreciate it from the audience."

"A wise decision. I should hate to discover that you have hidden musical talents as well. My professional reputation might never recover."

You find a seat and enjoy the performance over a mug of ale. Emma plays magnificently, moving from lively dances to tender ballads, occasionally catching your eye with a small, conspiratorial smile.

When the applause finally dies away, she gives you a theatrical bow.

"Thank you for your patronage, Signor Fibonacci. Your contribution to the arts has been invaluable."

after_performance.text:
The evening proves unexpectedly entertaining. You carry drinks, collect musical requests, and persuade a particularly enthusiastic merchant that standing directly in front of the violinist to declare his admiration is not strictly necessary.

Meanwhile, Emma performs with astonishing skill. She moves effortlessly between solemn melodies and lively dances, captivating the entire room. Even the innkeeper abandons his accounts to listen.

At one point, a rather tipsy gentleman insists that he knows a traditional dance from his homeland. Emma obligingly begins playing, and you watch him demonstrate something resembling a goose attempting to escape a sack.

Emma manages to finish the tune without laughing.

Barely.

By the time the last guests depart, the wooden bowl is overflowing with coins. Emma sits beside you at an empty table and begins counting, arranging the money into neat little stacks.

"Well! That was considerably more profitable than expected."

She separates a generous portion of the earnings, then retrieves a card from the little case beside her violin.

"Now, Antonio, you've earned your share. One hundred gold, if you'd prefer something practical."

She places the card next to the coins.

"Or this. A spare creation of mine. Rather a clever little enchantment, if I say so myself."

She smiles.

"And I generally do."

parameters.text:
"I'll take the money, thank you. I've acquired a rather expensive habit of attending the Academy."

"An appalling habit. I suffer from precisely the same affliction."

Emma pushes the coins toward you.

"One hundred gold, as promised. You've earned every piece."

She gathers the remaining coins into her purse, looking thoroughly satisfied.

"An excellent evening's work, Fibonacci. Perhaps we should go into business together."

"I'll take the card. Money comes and goes, but a good enchantment is worth keeping."

Emma looks pleased.

"An intelligent choice. Although I should point out that money has the considerable advantage of being accepted by bakers."

She hands you the card, watching with quiet satisfaction as you examine her work.

"I made that one last term. It served me rather well, but I've since improved upon the design."

"You're giving me your discarded experiments?"

"My _surplus masterpieces_, Antonio. There's a difference."

She smiles.

"Do take good care of it."

after_performance.title: A Profitable Evening

title: A Standing Engagement
text:
"Antonio! Just the man I was looking for."

Emma approaches you with a particularly satisfied expression. Evidently, something has gone her way.

"Remember our little musical enterprise? Well, I've received an offer from the Old Monk Inn. They want me to perform every Friday evening. Regular pay, generous tips, and apparently an audience with excellent taste."

She pauses, smiling.

"Naturally, I accepted. But I'd much rather concentrate on the violin than spend half the evening chasing drunken merchants for their unpaid bills."

She regards you thoughtfully.

"So, what do you say to making our partnership official? Every Friday evening, a few hours of honest work, and we divide the earnings. I provide the artistic talent, you provide the indispensable logistical support."

Her smile turns mischievous.

"An exceptionally fair arrangement, wouldn't you agree?"

parameters.text:
"Why not? We made a pretty good team last time."

"Excellent! I knew you were a man of sound judgment."

Emma looks delighted.

"Friday evenings, then. The Old Monk Inn. I'll speak to the innkeeper and make the arrangements."

She begins to leave, then turns back.

"Oh, and Antonio? If anyone asks, you're my _manager_. It sounds so much more distinguished than 'the fellow who carries the drinks.'"

job.name: Musical Evenings with Emma
job.description: Every Friday evening at the Old Monk Inn: Emma provides the violin, you provide the logistical support.

parameters.text: "I've been looking over the Friday performance arrangements," Emma says. "It's rather pleasant having a partner who understands that music involves rather more than appearing onstage." You remind her that you agreed to help. "And I haven't forgotten." She smiles. "If the evenings go well, I may even allow you to claim a small share of the glory. The administrative glory, naturally."

"I'm afraid I can't commit to every Friday evening. Academy life keeps me busy enough already."

"Of course. A demanding scholarly career must come first."

Emma nods, entirely untroubled.

"I'll find someone else to help. Perhaps a young man with fewer ambitions and a greater appreciation for carrying trays."

She gives you a teasing smile.

"Still, you must come and listen sometime. I promise not to charge you admission."

"I've sorted out the Friday performances," Emma tells you. "I found another way to manage the arrangements, so you needn't worry about not being available." You thank her for understanding. "Of course I understand. You have your own commitments." Her expression brightens. "Though you are still permitted to come and listen. I shall endeavor to make it worth your time."

text:
Emma finds you after lunch with a folded itinerary in one hand and the expression of someone about to make an offer you would be foolish to refuse.

"I have decided to take up riding," she announces. "It seems one cannot move in distinguished circles without eventually being expected to sit on a horse. I refuse to have my future ruined by a saddle."

"A sound academic concern."

"Quite. I've arranged two horses, equipment, and an afternoon's excursion through the countryside. The stablemaster assures me the animals are exceptionally docile." She pauses. "I thought you might like to come."

She offers you the itinerary, then draws it back before you can unfold it. "And before you ask: yes, I could go alone. I simply think your company might improve the experience. Don't make me regret saying so."

parameters.text:
"How could I refuse an opportunity to see you conquer yet another discipline?"

"You are welcome to admire my progress from a safe distance," Emma says. "Ideally from a horse that is slower than mine."

She slips the itinerary into her pocket, looking quite pleased despite herself.

You thank her, but tell her you have other plans this afternoon.

"Of course." She folds the itinerary with unnecessary precision. "I'll have to face the perils of respectable society without you."

Her smile returns. "If I return speaking exclusively about bloodlines and hunting parties, please intervene."

She leaves for the stables. It occurs to you that she had already arranged the outing for two.

"Apparently Emma Delamain has taken up riding," your companion remarks. "She says it's useful for making connections in society. Though she did admit the countryside was rather lovely. I suspect she's discovered a pastime she enjoys."

title: A Most Useful Afternoon

emma_the_ride.text:
The first stretch of the ride is glorious. Beyond the Academy's fields, the road winds between golden meadows and low stone walls. The dark line of the Schlupak forest lies across the distant hills. Emma sits remarkably straight in her saddle, watching the stablemaster's lesson pay off with each passing minute.

"Well?" she asks, guiding her horse alongside yours. "Do I look as if I belong at a country estate?"

You are still considering your answer when your horse decides to investigate a particularly interesting rut. The world tilts. Your boots lose their stirrups, and you land in the grass with a thud that thoroughly extinguishes any aristocratic aspirations you might have entertained.

"Antonio!"

Emma is off her horse almost before you have caught your breath. She drops to her knees beside you, one hand on your shoulder, the other hovering anxiously near your face. "Are you hurt? Where? Look at me."

You manage to assure her that you are whole, if somewhat less dignified. Only then does she exhale. Her fingers remain on your shoulder a moment longer than necessary.

{{almost_kiss}}

From the direction of the forest comes a long, wavering howl. Another answers it. Emma's horse jerks its head, tears free of the reins she has dropped, and bolts straight toward the trees. Your own horse, apparently possessed of better judgment, gallops back toward the Academy.

For a moment, you both stare after them.

"Well," Emma says faintly. "The stablemaster did say they were docile. He neglected to specify under what circumstances."

"Wolves?"

"Likely far away. But my horse is heading into Schlupak, and I'm responsible for him." She rises and brushes the grass from her skirts. "We have to find him."

parameters.text:
You study the churned earth at the forest edge. The horse's prints are easy to distinguish from older tracks, and broken fern stems reveal where he left the path. You lead Emma along a winding but reliable trail.

"A convincing performance," she admits. "If your artificery career fails, you might consider becoming a bloodhound."

You follow a promising trail until it disappears in a patch of stones. A detour, two mistaken hoofprints, and a spirited disagreement about moss later, you finally hear contented chewing ahead.

"If we ever become lost together," Emma says, "I shall insist we disagree in a more orderly fashion."

You sprint beneath the branches, vault a fallen log, and keep the flash of the horse's pale tail in sight. Emma follows, refusing to be left behind. You slow at last when the animal stops in a sunlit clearing.

Emma catches her breath beside you. "An excellent demonstration of speed. I trust you'll never ask me to applaud it while running."

The first hundred paces go splendidly. The next hundred convince you that horses possess a rather unfair advantage in the matter of legs. You lose him among the trees and spend a good while searching with Emma before a suspiciously satisfied snort gives him away.

"Your dedication is admirable," Emma says, supporting herself against a tree. "Your pace was, eventually, negotiable."

emma_the_ride.title: An Undignified Dismount

variants.text: You reach for the hand against your cheek. Emma notices, and for once has nothing clever to say. She is very close. Her gaze slips briefly to your lips; you lean toward one another, slowly enough that either of you could stop. Neither does—until the howl cuts through the afternoon.

almost_kiss.fallback: "You frightened me," she says, unexpectedly quiet. Then she notices her hand still resting on you and withdraws it. "Next time you wish to impress me, Antonio, I recommend remaining on the horse."

emma_honey_clearing.text:
The runaway stands in a clearing, entirely untroubled by his adventure. He has discovered a fallen, honey-filled comb beside an old hollow tree and is happily devouring its contents. Golden drops cling to his muzzle.

Emma steps forward, then freezes. "Antonio. Is that _Schlupak honey_?"

It is. Rare forest bees produce it in tiny quantities, and artificers prize it as a powerful crafting ingredient. A modest fortune is disappearing into a horse with no appreciation of market prices.

The horse looks up, chews thoughtfully, and goes back for more.

parameters.text:
"He's had quite a fright," you say. "Let him finish."

Emma looks from the comb to the horse, then to you. "You do realize what he's eating?"

"Every expensive mouthful."

She smiles, and reaches out to stroke the animal's neck. "I suppose he deserves a little comfort. And perhaps we do, too."

"Hold his reins," you tell Emma. "We can still rescue some of it."

While she calms the horse, you carefully collect three intact portions of the honeycomb. The animal watches your work with an expression of deep personal betrayal.

"A sound investment," Emma concedes, eyeing your prize. "Though I suspect he will never forgive you."

optionTemplates.text: Admire the world's most expensive snack

parameters.text:
By the time you reach him, the last useful drop has vanished. The horse stands amid the wreckage of a small fortune, honey dripping from his whiskers.

"We've been robbed," you say.

"By a creature that cannot count," Emma replies. She tries to maintain a severe expression. The horse sneezes. Emma bursts out laughing, and you soon join her, both of you helpless before the spectacle.

"Well," she says at last, wiping her eyes, "at least someone has had a profitable afternoon."

emma_honey_clearing.title: The Sweetest Crime

emma_ride_home.text:
Emma takes the reins, and together you guide the horse back to the path. With your own mount long gone, there is only one sensible way home: you share the saddle, Emma in front and you behind her, keeping the horse at a gentle walk.

The afternoon light turns amber over the fields. Emma occasionally points out a distant farmhouse or a peculiar shape in the clouds, but there are stretches when neither of you feels the need to speak. The road is narrow, the saddle is not designed for two, and every bend brings you a little closer together.

"I must say, Antonio, you're proving to be a remarkably comfortable riding accessory."

"Accessory?"

"Yes. A little bulky, perhaps, but quite effective at keeping me warm." She pauses, then adds sharply, "And before you say whatever disgraceful thing has just occurred to you, don't."

"I haven't said anything!"

"Precisely. I'd like to preserve that happy state of affairs."

You hear the smile in her voice. A moment later, she settles back against you, apparently deciding that her riding accessory might as well be put to good use.

"I had intended this excursion to improve my prospects in society," she says eventually. "Instead I've lost a horse, nearly lost you, and discovered that equestrian training involves rather more running than advertised."

"A wasted afternoon, then?"

"Not at all." She rests one hand lightly over yours for a moment. "I think I'd like to do something equally impractical again."

As the Academy comes into view, she straightens in the saddle. "Naturally, we shall tell the stablemaster that everything went precisely according to plan."

parameters.text: Emma gives you a sidelong look. "I was considering another outing. Somewhere with fewer wolves, perhaps." You ask whether horses are included. "Only if you promise to remain on yours this time." She smiles. "Though I admit the journey back wasn't entirely unpleasant."

emma_ride_home.title: The Long Way Home

text:
Your third artificery lesson is progressing remarkably well. You've arranged your ingredients, prepared your pigments, and even managed to follow most of the professor's instructions. At this rate, you might produce something almost respectable.

Then your elbow catches a jar.

A cascade of shimmering blue powder spills across the workbench, mixing with your carefully prepared ingredients. You grab for a cloth, knock over a second jar, and watch in horror as the entire mixture begins to glow.

There is a sharp pop, a flash of blue light, and the unmistakable smell of burnt cinnamon.

When the smoke clears, a perfectly formed card lies in the middle of the table.

You pick it up cautiously. The enchantments woven into its surface are unlike anything you've seen before: intricate, powerful, and somehow perfectly balanced.

The professor approaches, examines your creation, and falls silent.

"Fibonacci. How exactly did you achieve this?"

An excellent question. One you would very much like to know the answer to yourself.

"Remarkable," the professor murmurs. "Quite remarkable. You must document your procedure."

Yes. Of course. Your procedure.

You glance at the empty jars, the stained workbench, and the smoking remains of your notes.

This could be difficult.
title: Happy Little Accident

text:
Professor Lombard is about to start her class when the classroom door opens. The Academy's administrator enters, carrying a large ledger and looking as though he has come to collect money. You instinctively check your purse.

"Ah, excellent timing!" Lombard exclaims. "Ladies and gentlemen, a little announcement before we start."

The administrator adjusts his spectacles.

"The Academy's first league season of the academic year begins today. As is tradition, each student shall face every other student exactly once in an official match. Victories will earn points toward the league standings, and the student finishing first shall receive a prize in recognition of their achievement."

That gets everyone's attention.

"The league is an important part of your education," Glützenbaum adds enthusiastically. "A chance to test your creations, exercise your strategic abilities, and demonstrate your progress. And remember, you will be competing with the very cards you craft and enchant during your studies!"

Around the room, the reactions are decidedly mixed. Emma sits a little straighter, her green eyes bright with unmistakable determination. Beside her, Vaiana yawns extravagantly, apparently finding the prospect of an entire season of competition rather exhausting. Ousmane slowly twirls his magnificent moustache, contemplating the announcement with the serene confidence of a general surveying a battlefield.

Molly, meanwhile, looks rather less enthusiastic. She glances around at her classmates, then down at her modest deck, visibly calculating just how many defeats she might be expected to endure.

"Your first official matches may begin this afternoon," the administrator concludes. "Choose your opponents, prepare your decks, and may the best artificer win."

"Splendid!" Lombard claps his hands. "Nothing like a little healthy competition to encourage academic excellence! Do try to remain on speaking terms with one another."

You survey your fellow students. Several are already exchanging challenging looks.

Apparently, your education is about to become considerably more interesting.
title: The Ligue Starts
An Invitation to the Workshop
text:
The morning's artificery lesson has barely begun when a tremendous clatter erupts from the corridor.

Professor Lombard stops mid-sentence. A metallic crash follows, then a booming voice.

"Nothing broken! Nothing important, anyway!"

The classroom door swings open, admitting a mountain of a man in a battered leather apron. His sleeves are rolled above enormous forearms, his thick black beard is dusted with soot, and a collection of tools jangles from his belt. He carries a curious brass contraption under one arm and wears the broad, cheerful grin of someone having an exceptionally good morning.

"Morning, Professor! Borrow your students for a minute?"

Lombard regards the visitor, then the faint trail of oily footprints he has left across the floor.

"Provided you don't dismantle anything, Frank."

"Wouldn't dream of it!"

Frank deposits his contraption on the nearest desk. It unfolds with a series of clicks into a delicate arrangement of brass rings surrounding a blue crystal. The crystal begins to glow.

"Right, then! Name's Frank. I run the Academy workshop, down by the old foundry. Some of you have probably heard the hammering. Those who haven't should consider having their ears examined."

A few students laugh.

"Now, you're learning to make cards in here, and fine things they are. But artificery doesn't begin and end with a bit of enchanted paper. There's a whole world of useful things you can build with your own two hands!"

He taps the brass contraption affectionately.

"**Artifacts.** Tools, totems, trinkets. A good tool can help you craft better cards. A well-made totem can give you an advantage during a match. And a clever little trinket? Well, you'd be surprised how often the right contraption can get you out of trouble."

He gives the crystal a twist. The brass rings spin faster, producing a pleasant musical hum.

"Of course, making these things takes more than a strong arm and a hammer. You'll need to understand the magical colors you're working with. Pay attention in your lessons, study hard, learn from your classmates. The more you know, the more ambitious your creations can become."

The humming abruptly becomes a high-pitched whistle.

Frank frowns at the contraption.

"Ah. That's new."

He gives it a firm tap. The whistling stops.

"There we are! Now, I've got a few simple patterns ready for beginners. Nothing too fancy, but enough to get you started. You can come by the workshop whenever you like, pick a pattern, and have a go at making something."

He raises a thick, grease-stained finger.

"**One rule, though: you bring your own materials.** I'll provide the benches, the tools, and whatever advice I can shout at you. But iron, copper, crystals, and the rest? That's your responsibility. Can't have you lot emptying my stores every time you get an idea."

"An eminently sensible policy," Lombard observes.

"Had to introduce it after the last lot," Frank replies darkly. "You wouldn't believe how much brass a determined student can waste."

He folds the contraption back into its casing, tucks it under his arm, and heads for the door.

"Anyway, you're all welcome! Don't worry if you've never held a hammer. We'll soon put that right. And remember: the first rule of engineering is that if something doesn't work, you've learned one way not to build it!"

He pauses in the doorway.

"Second rule: if it starts ticking and you didn't put a clock in it, come and fetch me."

With a hearty laugh, he disappears into the corridor.

Professor Lombard surveys the class, waits for the last of the chuckles to subside, and returns to the blackboard.

"Now, where were we? Ah, yes. The importance of precise measurements."

You glance at the door.

The workshop certainly sounds worth a visit.

parameters.title: The Master Engineer
parameters.description: Frank runs the Academy workshop, where students can craft artifacts using their own materials and knowledge of magical colors. A burly, cheerful, hardworking engineer with a thick black beard, a booming voice, and a practical approach to teaching. He provides beginner patterns and welcomes students to the workshop at any time.

title: A Few Patterns to Get You Started
text:
The Academy workshop smells of hot metal, sawdust, and something faintly sweet that is probably best left unidentified. Tools hang in neat rows above crowded benches. Along one wall, a collection of unfinished contraptions clicks, hums, and occasionally shudders.

Frank stands at an anvil, holding a small piece of metal in a pair of tongs. He spots you, breaks into a grin, and sets it aside.

"There you are! Come in, come in. Mind the bucket."

You step around a bucket full of bent brass rods.

"Other bucket."

You narrowly avoid a second one.

"Excellent. Good awareness of your surroundings. Essential workshop skill."

He wipes his hands on his apron and clears a space on the nearest bench, shifting an alarming quantity of metal with one enormous forearm. From a drawer, he produces four rolled sheets of thick paper.

"Now, I promised you a few patterns. **Three tools and a trinket.** Simple enough to start with, useful enough to keep."

He spreads out the first sheet and holds its curling corners down with a hammer and a mug.

"**Basic Stabilisator.** Keeps the matter you're working with steady while you shape it. Helps with precision, gives you a little more mastery over the work. Black magic, a bit of silver, and a steady hand. Preferably yours."

The next sheet is covered in neatly ruled diagrams and cramped annotations.

"**Basic Codex.** Helps you keep track of the crafting process. What you've done, what comes next, which step you were absolutely certain you could skip. Good for your erudition. You'll need blue magic and some mox for that one."

He unrolls the third pattern, revealing a curious arrangement of small apertures.

"**Basic Porticuli.** Gives you glimpses of what might be possible. Handy when you're short on inspiration. Red magic and magic dust. Don't spend all afternoon peering into it, though. At some point you've got to actually make something."

The final sheet bears the drawing of an amulet.

"And a **Vitality Amulet**. A little something to put a bit more life in you. Green magic, magic dust. Useful outside the workshop, too. Especially if your idea of lunch is whatever you can eat while running to your next lesson."

He gathers the four patterns and pushes them towards you.

"These are yours. No charge for the patterns. **Materials are still your responsibility**, mind. Each one takes a hundred gold's worth of supplies, plus five of the material marked on the sheet. You'll need a proper grasp of its color, too."

You look over the diagrams. They seem considerably less simple now that they are in front of you.

Frank notices your expression.

"Don't worry about making all four at once. Pick something you can manage and take it one step at a time. Read the pattern before you start, measure before you cut, and ask if you're unsure."

Something behind him gives a sharp metallic ping.

Without looking round, Frank reaches back and catches a small brass wheel.

"And keep an eye on your surroundings."

He drops the wheel into the first bucket and gives you a cheerful nod.

"Right, then. Let's see what you can make!"
